reviews.review: 9/10 great game. Feels like good SF movie. I also liked the ending and multiplayer concept. Works well on Windows 10, requiers Origins account. Does not include DLCs which are expensive.

I havent experienced the problems mentioned by others, and the game looks gorgeous. i would suggest grabbing the free DLC from Origin if you didnt get the DLC pack here, playing the multiplayer will affect the story mode in certain ways. i got this game from EA Play.

Mass Effect 3 is an extremely flawed game, most of it's flaws stemming from the fact that EA (who else?) rushed it out, and it shows.

Models are constantly clipping through each other, not attaching to each other when they should, and the animations just show a general lack of polish.

The companion selection is pitiful. Not a single companion introduced in ME2 made it into ME3 as more than a cameo. Or at most, a few of them have a brief role in the story, but still never join you as companions. And this problem leaks out into other aspects of the game. If certain characters were available as companions, some key decisions in the game would have a lot more stake to them, which would have made it a lot more tense, and made the payoff a lot better.

In addition, there is one much more massive problem. In, mind you, a ROLE PLAYING GAME, almost all of the dialogue is from on-rails cut scenes. 
Dialogue options are rare, and even when you get one, almost every single dialogue choice has been reduced to 2 options. Say the nice thing, or say the mean thing.
I cannot truly express how terrible this is. In the previous two games, dialogue choices were plentiful and had some amount of depth, usually including a 3rd, neutral option, or even a 4th option. But now the system is shallow and terrible, and I blame EA for this.

And, of course, you've all probably heard of the fabled ending, even if you've never played a Mass Effect game.
I all honesty, I can personally say that the ending...  wasn't that bad. And I feel like a lot of people at least somewhat agree. I mean, when ME3 came out, everyone was furious at the ending, but now that it's been 8 years, everyone seems to have calmed down a bit, and realized that the ending isn't TOO bad.
Mind you, it still is nowhere near as good as fans would've liked, but my only criticism is that I personally wanted a bit MORE of an epilogue.

But, by now, you're probably wondering why I'm still recommending this game, so I'll get to the pros right now.

The combat itself is the best in the series They've introduced a new combat roll mechanic, which works pretty well, even though it's assigned to the same key as 'run' and 'take cover'. In ME3, you're now allowed to carry all types of weapons, no matter your class, though each weapon has a weight, and the more your total weapons weigh, the slower your powers recharge. This system actually allows you to customize your character a lot more than in the previous 2 games.

Tying into my previous point, the enemy design is also really great! There are 3 different factions you fight throughout the game, and each enemy on each faction serves a specific purpose.
For the most part, there are 3 different purposes that a type of enemy can serve. There are basic foot soldiers who are just used as cannon fodder, there are enemies the force you into cover (such as the ATLAS mechs, the ravangers, and the geth rocket troopers), and enemies that try to flush you from cover (such as the phantoms, the banshees, and the geth hunters).
These main 3 enemy varieties force you to make tactical decisions on the spot about who to kill first, where should I get to cover, what you should use your powers on.
In addition, some enemies serve another purpose, such the centurions, which can throw smoke grenades, or mauraders, which buff other enemies.

And though the dialogue choices are terrible, the writing itself is great! All of the characters feel so much more real then in the previous games, especially in their interactions with each other. All of your companions actually act like friends around each other, and it's great!

And, surprisingly enough, the tacked on multiplayer mode is genuinely fun, despite the lootbox mechanic. It's a PVE, so I feel like the lootbox system works better than it should have.

And the DLC is well worth the hefty price, and I highly suggest you get it. Even just for the citadel DLC alone, which is fantastic.

Anyways, this has been my long winded ME3 rant. Thank you for coming to my Ted Talk.

Origin's launcher doesn't actually work with Steam. I went as far as to factory reset my PC so I know that the issue is not with my computer, my settings, or my configuration. If you buy this game and it's DLC, you are spending $60 for a game from 2012 that does not launch. Only $30 of that is refundable. I love this game so much, but nobody should ever buy it

I had a huge journey through the trilogy, and connected each of them through my playthrough. From the first Mass Effect, to Mass Effect 2, and now Mass Effect 3. This game is truly a unforgettable experience to those that wishes to see through to the end. This game will always be about Shepard through the trilogy. Both how he started, and how he ended. Many references comes around as you play through, and it usually rings a bell whenever anything is mentioned from the previous game.

Dont get this, if you want a true experience then get the first game, at LEAST the second. If you beat the first game, it gets better as you play through the other 2. If you get this now, you wont get it and even if you do, your character wont mention much about what has happened, your own experience, your own choices you made in the past that caused it. Gameplay is third person shooter games and you team up in groups of 3. You lead the 2 teams as a Commander. Theres choices in this game, and if you had played the past games then you should know every choice you made in the past will be brought up to this game when you import your previous save file.

Theres really alot going on in this game, along with the past 2 games. Through the time I played in Steam, there was only 2 games and it hurts me because I want to know how MY story ends. But finally, this game is out and I finally get to see how my story ended. I liked it, and I had both good and bad moments through the time (involving my choices, which sometimes I feel I regret it but then come to understanding), but its overall an amazing story.

As mentioned, do NOT get this if you want to understand the full story. It'll also make more interesting if you do beat the first 2 games since as mentioned, you can import your save file and everything you had done in the past games will be mentioned. Alongside Mass Effect 2 should you beat the first Mass Effect.

Whatever choice you make is up to you, but I strongly suggest getting all 3. Mainly because you get to have your own story on how you want it. How you see fit.
